phase: Vihu Cards Adopt Real TCG Print Standards
milestone: The World Card half of item #4 of a new six-item governing request: 'For vihu cards printing (magic cards, world cards and whatsoever card we introduce in future), follow TCG standards.' -- js/magicCardArt.js's Magic Card gets the identical, hand-mirrored treatment (see root build-info.json's own entry for the full account).
slice: tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js's _drawCardFront/_drawCardBack now render at genuine TCG (Trading Card Game) print-industry standards -- a true 2.5in x 3.5in 'poker size' trim (matching Magic: The Gathering / Pokemon / Yu-Gi-Oh's own real physical card size), 300 DPI (this codebase's own established Publish Quality print-vendor minimum), and a 1/8in die-cut corner radius -- instead of an arbitrary screen-only 700x980 canvas, mirrored byte-for-byte from the sibling js/magicCardArt.js implementation kept in lockstep by hand per this codebase's own established 'no cross-tool sharing, mirror instead' discipline. New constants (CARD_PRINT_DPI=300, CARD_TRIM_IN_W/H=2.5/3.5, CARD_PIXEL_W/H=750/1050, CARD_RENDER_SCALE=750/700, CARD_CORNER_RADIUS derived from the 0.125in die-cut spec) are added alongside the unchanged CARD_ART_W/H=700/980 logical coordinate space; both draw functions now set canvas.width/height to the true CARD_PIXEL_W/H and call ctx.scale(CARD_RENDER_SCALE, CARD_RENDER_SCALE) immediately after getting the 2D context -- one uniform transform maps every existing hand-tuned drawing call onto the larger device pixel buffer with zero coordinate changes needed anywhere in either function. Every hardcoded corner-radius literal (36, 34) is replaced with CARD_CORNER_RADIUS (or CARD_CORNER_RADIUS-2 for the inset border stroke). A pre-existing sibling regression script for this file, card_platform/verify_card_art.js (dated before this sprint), was found stale and fixed in the same pass: a Playwright route() pattern with no trailing wildcard never matched a request URL carrying this codebase's own '?v=NNNN' cache-bust query string (empirically proven via a dedicated diagnostic script, not assumed), silently letting the real, network-blocked-in-this-sandbox modules load instead of the mocks; the mock's own getIdentity() reported signedIn:false, which correctly hid the entire Welcome screen behind World Builder v2's real Mandatory Sign-In gate; a stale '700x980' canvas-dimension assertion, updated to the new, correct 750x1050 -- the disclosed, intended consequence of this sprint's own upgrade; and a star-pixel-sampling assertion that computed its sample coordinate in the old 700-wide logical space and handed it directly to ctx.getImageData (which always reads raw device pixels, unaffected by ctx.scale) -- coincidentally passing by landing inside an unrelated star's own glow radius, not genuinely verifying the intended coordinate -- fixed by scaling the sample coordinate by CARD_RENDER_SCALE before sampling. Now passes 12/12, alongside the new, decisive tcg_card_verify.js suite (14/14, covering both Magic Card and World Card together). Full regression: both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged, confirming zero impact on either Builder-tooling surface. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js.
